title: Second Sitting of 2nd Session of 2025
summary: The sitting ran from 9:02 to 9:47. After the Speaker announced the death of a former Gaddhoo MP, debate on the bill amending the Civil Aviation Authority Act wrapped up and the bill was accepted and sent to the National Development and Heritage Committee. The House then approved three presidential nominations after committee reports: a non-resident ambassador to Nepal and two Supreme Court judges. The text layer is partly garbled, so the opening attendance figures are less certain than the vote counts.

items.title: Attendance of the sitting
items.outcome: announced by the chair: 37 present, 9 on leave, 3 on official travel

items.title: Adoption of minutes of sittings 28 to 32 of the first session of 2025
items.outcome: no amendments submitted; accepted by the chair

items.title: Speaker's announcement: death of former Gaddhoo MP Ahmed Rasheed
items.outcome: condolences given; members asked to stand for a moment of silence

items.title: Bill amending the Maldives Civil Aviation Authority Act (Act 2/2012), debate continued
items.outcome: debate concluded; accepted 59-1; sent to the National Development and Heritage Committee

items.title: Foreign Relations Committee report on appointing the ambassador to India as non-resident ambassador to Nepal
Judicial Committee report on appointing two Supreme Court judges
items.outcome: debated; Abdulla Hameed approved 60-0 and Mohamed Saleem approved 61-0

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supports the amendment but warns that airport safety checks and reports were not reliable, and that the responsible bodies must enforce the rules properly.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Says the amendment will make the authority responsible for regional airport equipment and fencing, and urges members to vote for the bill without politicising it.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: As Foreign Relations Committee rapporteur, presents the report finding the nominee qualified; the committee passed it unanimously.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Fully supports the committee report, citing the nominee's long diplomatic career and the cost advantage of using an ambassador already in the region.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: As Judicial Committee rapporteur, presents the report finding both Supreme Court nominees meet the constitutional requirements; the committee passed it unanimously.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Backs the nominees, citing the committee's vetting, and calls on the MDP to vote for them so the vote passes by consensus.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Questions how the seats were vacated and the independence of the new judges, saying the earlier removal of judges was not lawful; the chair told him to sit down.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 28 to 32 of the first session of 2025 were accepted by the chair.
The Civil Aviation Authority Act amendment bill was accepted 59-1 and sent to the National Development and Heritage Committee.
The House approved the appointment of the ambassador to India as non-resident ambassador to Nepal, 59-0.
The House approved Abdulla Hameed as a Supreme Court judge, 60-0.
The House approved Mohamed Saleem as a Supreme Court judge, 61-0.
Next sitting set for Monday 16 June 2025 at 9:00.
